Critically, a load- or resource-driven origin (H4, and the capacity variant) is separated from H1 only by resource metrics — if pricing-engine CPU/mem/GC shows a step at 12:04 the ranking holds but is partly attributable to capacity; if resources stay flat while latency steps, H1's "slow code path" reading strengthens. challenges.issue: Temporal coincidence is strong (flag at 12:04:00Z, first bad bucket 12:04-12:06), but the MECHANISM hop — 'greeks_v2 on all traffic slows the quote path' — rests on an unverified assumption. A persistent, non-spiky 2.6s p99 sustained ~2h is as consistent with capacity saturation as with a heavy flag path; the two are not separated by any available datum.

Given it precedes onset by 8 minutes, keeping it at 0.10 while H4 sits at 0.16 is a close call, though not blocking.

redis-cache has never been measured: no latency/error/hit-rate/failover data for a component that is the ONLY shared node across the affected services and is the origin named in precedent HIST-107. It is not 'contradicted' — it is unassessed, and it names a DIFFERENT origin and fix than H1. This is the main gap blocking a confident single-origin conclusion.

Grounding is verified at every hop: the flag lands in the first anomalous pricing-engine bucket (F1/F9/F15/F22); pricing-engine logs name the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo path as the budget-overrun source, with the first WARN at 12:05:21Z — after the flag — and no earlier greeks_v2-adjacent error (F30/F32), persisting unabated to 13:58 (F31); CPU steps in the same bucket with error_rate rising 0.24%->8.5%->13% (F24/F25/F26/F33); request_rate and memory stay flat, excluding load-driven and memory-driven origins (F27/F28); order-service's sole error signature is its direct pricing-engine call timing out ~2 min later (F2/F3/F16). Alternatives are tested and contradicted: H2 is not on the failing hop, shows no MDS anomaly, and precedes onset by 8 min (F4/F16/F18); H3 is flat on every measurable redis metric with a matching historical profile explicitly checked (F34/F12), and redis exposes no latency/error telemetry — a permanently unavailable source, not an untested one; H4 has no traffic step (F28) and is contradicted by the per-request greeks_v2 log attribution. Remaining softness is secondary, not ranking-relevant: no revert-with-recovery A/B (flag never reverted; a revert is a mitigation, not a query), CPU/latency co-located only within 3-4 min buckets (no sub-bucket ordering available), no GC metric exposed (F29), and part of the latency is attributable to CPU ceiling rather than purely code-path cost. Confidence on origin is high; the residual uncertainty is on mechanism attribution, which does not change the fix.
